title: Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_695
description: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. The Fysbis malware is known to be a modular Linux trojan/backdoor that implements plug-in and controller modules as distinct classes. It includes both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of ELF binaries and can install itself with or without root privileges. Your goal is to identify and investigate the suspicious activity, determine the extent of the compromise, and take appropriate containment measures.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a potential compromise involving the Sofacy group's Fysbis backdoor on a Linux-based network. The Fysbis malware is known to be a modular Linux trojan/backdoor that implements plug-in and controller modules as distinct classes. It includes both 32-bit and 64-bit versions of ELF binaries and can install itself with or without root privileges. Your goal is to identify and investigate the suspicious activity, determine the extent of the compromise, and take appropriate containment measures.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.
levels.local_content: Access the target host via SSH using the following credentials: Username: cyrano, Password: cyrano. Enter 'start' to begin the investigation.

levels.title: Suspicious Service Discovery
levels.content: While monitoring the network, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate the target host to identify any unauthorized or suspicious services running on the system.
levels.solution: To identify suspicious services, you can use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services. Look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations. The suspicious service in this scenario is `systemkernelservicedefender.service`. Verify the service name in the provisioning files.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check the systemd services and look for any services that seem out of place or have unusual configurations.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-units --type=service` command to list all running services.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl status systemkernelservicedefender.service` command to check the status of the suspicious service.

levels.title: Persistence Discovery
levels.content: You have identified a suspicious service running on the target host. Determine how this service is automatically started after reboot.
levels.solution: To determine how the service is automatically started after reboot, you can examine the systemd service files and timers. The service `systemkernelservicedefender.service` is maintained by the timer `lab-checkin.timer`. Verify the persistence identifier in the provisioning files.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Examine the systemd service files and timers to understand how the service is maintained.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl list-timers` command to list all systemd timers.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl cat lab-checkin.timer` command to view the contents of the timer file.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: Investigate the network traffic associated with the suspicious service to determine which network port is used for the suspicious communication.
levels.solution: To investigate the network traffic associated with the suspicious service, you can use network monitoring tools to capture and analyze the traffic from the suspicious service. The suspicious communication is using port 80. Verify the C2 port number in the provisioning files.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to capture and analyze the traffic from the suspicious service.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Use the `netstat -tuln` command to list all network connections.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: Use the `ss -tuln` command to list all network connections and check for port 80.
